# International Criminal Court (ICC)

> > The International Criminal Court is an independent permanent tribunal investigating and prosecuting individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of aggression.

The ICC operates under the Rome Statute with 123 States Parties, working alongside the Assembly of States Parties (ASP) and Trust Fund for Victims. The Court conducts investigations and trials in situations worldwide, including cases from Ukraine, Democratic Republic of Congo, and the Philippines, while upholding international justice and victims' rights.

## Key Topics

- International Criminal Court (ICC)
- Rome Statute
- Genocide
- War crimes
- Crimes against humanity
- Crime of aggression
- Assembly of States Parties (ASP)
- Trust Fund for Victims
- Victims reparations
- Court investigations
- International justice
- Situations under investigation (Ukraine, DRC, Philippines)
- State cooperation
- Complementarity principle
